1	# Requirements Quality Checklist: P-RF09 — Settings Dashboard
2	
3	**Purpose**: Risk-weighted requirements-quality review of spec.md, covering the three functional areas (dashboard chart/narrative, account deletion/LGPD, profile+biometric+logout) plus cross-cutting consistency, with extra depth on the two highest-risk areas: account deletion (irreversible, legally sensitive per RNF05) and dashboard aggregation (the most conditional/edge-case-heavy logic).
4	**Created**: 2026-10-24
5	**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)
6	
7	**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
8	**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
9	**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.
10	
11	## Account Deletion & Data Lifecycle (LGPD / RNF05)
12	
13	- [ ] CHK001 Is "every piece of data tied to it" (RNF05) enumerated as a concrete, exhaustive list of locally-held data categories (session, cached profile, entries, chat, other), rather than left to an open-ended "any other locally held user data" phrase? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019, §SC-003]
14	- [ ] CHK002 Does the spec specify whether vault/PIN and biometric-preference local storage are included in or excluded from the account-deletion data wipe, given they are a separate on-device concern from the account itself? [Gap, Spec §FR-019]
15	- [ ] CHK003 Is the requirement for a second concurrent delete attempt (FR-022) scoped to "Apagar tudo" specifically, and does the spec confirm no other in-flight request (e.g., a profile save) is expected to block or race with an account-deletion request? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-022]
16	- [ ] CHK004 Does the spec define the dialog's behavior if the session expires while the delete-confirmation dialog is already open and the user has not yet tapped "Apagar tudo" vs. after tapping it but before the response resolves? [Edge Case, Spec Edge Cases]
17	- [ ] CHK005 Are the specific failure modes for `DELETE /account` (timeout, no connection, malformed response, expired session) each traceable to a distinct, non-overlapping user-facing outcome, or could two of them produce indistinguishable error text? [Consistency, Spec §FR-020]
18	- [ ] CHK006 Is "malformed response" for the delete call defined precisely enough (e.g., any non-success body) to be distinguished from "no response" so the retry-ability of each is unambiguous? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020]
19	- [ ] CHK007 Does SC-004 ("zero account deletions occur without explicit confirmation") have a corresponding requirement covering accidental dismissal (tap-outside, back-gesture, OS back button) as equivalent to "Cancelar", not merely the two button taps? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-021, §SC-004]
20	- [ ] CHK008 Is the irreversibility claim ("no way to undo it afterward") paired with a requirement stating there is no grace period, soft-delete, or recovery window on the backend side that the spec needs to account for? [Assumption, Spec User Story 2]
21	
22	## Dashboard Aggregation & Narrative
23	
24	- [ ] CHK009 Is the "roughly-equal time slices" bucketing rule (Assumptions) precise enough to be independently reproduced — i.e., does it specify how a non-evenly-divisible date range's remainder days are distributed among the ten bars? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec Assumptions]
25	- [ ] CHK010 Does the spec define expected behavior when the account's full date range is shorter than ten days (e.g., 3 days of history across >1 entries), beyond "naturally produces a chart with some empty bars"? [Edge Case, Spec Assumptions]
26	- [ ] CHK011 Is the boundary between the "exactly one entry" state (FR-004) and the "two or more entries" state (FR-005) specified in terms of the aggregate's entry count rather than UI appearance, so it cannot be misread as applying to bucket count instead? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, §FR-005]
27	- [ ] CHK012 Are all distinct dashboard states (empty, single-entry, multi-entry/narrative-pending, multi-entry/narrative-shown, narrative-unavailable, aggregate-error) individually named/identifiable so no two can be confused with each other in an implementation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003–FR-007]
28	- [ ] CHK013 Does the spec address what the chart area shows while the aggregate request is still in flight (a loading state), or is this left undefined between "nothing yet" and the first of the enumerated states? [Gap, Coverage]
29	- [ ] CHK014 Is retry behavior specified for the aggregate-error state (FR-007 says "with a way to retry") — e.g., does retrying re-request both the aggregate and, if it succeeds, the narrative, or only the aggregate? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007]
30	- [ ] CHK015 Does the spec distinguish, for narrative failures, between a narrative that fails outright and one that times out, or are both intentionally treated identically under "narrativa indisponível" with no behavioral difference? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006]
31	- [ ] CHK016 Is the requirement that the dashboard "MUST be recomputed from a fresh backend call every time Settings is opened" (FR-008) explicit about whether "opened" includes returning to Settings via back-navigation from a sub-screen, or only a fresh app-level navigation to it? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008]
32	
33	## Profile, Biometric Toggle & Sign-Out
34	
35	- [ ] CHK017 Is there a requirement guarding against a second concurrent name-save or biometric-toggle request analogous to FR-022's guard on "Sair"/"Apagar tudo", or is this double-submission case intentionally left uncovered for lower-risk actions? [Gap, Consistency, Spec §FR-022]
36	- [ ] CHK018 Is the display name's valid character set specified beyond a length bound (1–80 characters) — e.g., are whitespace-only names, emoji, or leading/trailing whitespace addressed? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
37	- [ ] CHK019 Does the spec define how the initials avatar is derived from a display name that has only one word, non-Latin characters, or is empty/default, so the avatar's content is unambiguous for every name state the spec allows? [Gap, Edge Case]
38	- [ ] CHK020 Is "the app's authentication entry point" (used identically by FR-016 and FR-019) defined with enough precision in the spec itself, or does it depend entirely on an external assumption resolved outside this spec's own requirements? [Traceability, Spec Assumptions, §FR-016, §FR-019]
39	- [ ] CHK021 Does the spec specify what the biometric toggle displays while its own save request is in flight (already-toggled optimistically vs. a pending/disabled state), distinct from the final success or revert-on-failure states in FR-013/FR-014? [Gap, Coverage]
40	
41	## Cross-Cutting Consistency & Traceability
42	
43	- [ ] CHK022 Are the generic failure phrases "timeout, no connection, malformed response" used across FR-007/FR-012/FR-014/FR-020 intended to cover every one of the backend's documented error codes (including rate-limiting), or could a code outside that phrase's literal scope produce an undefined outcome? [Completeness, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007, §FR-012, §FR-014, §FR-020]
44	- [ ] CHK023 Is the relationship between this spec's generic "existing expired-session handling... takes over exactly as it does elsewhere" (Edge Cases) and each individual FR's own failure-handling language made explicit, so a reader can tell session-expiry is an exception to FR-level retry/error requirements rather than a case those FRs also separately need to handle? [Consistency, Spec Edge Cases]
45	- [ ] CHK024 Do FR-016 (sign-out) and FR-019 (account deletion) each unambiguously state which locally held data categories they clear, such that their difference (entries/chat cache cleared only on deletion) is a requirement a reader can derive from the spec text alone, not just inferred from the two being adjacent? [Clarity, Consistency, Spec §FR-016, §FR-019]
46	- [ ] CHK025 Are success criteria SC-001 through SC-006 each traceable to at least one specific functional requirement and acceptance scenario, with no measurable outcome left floating without a corresponding testable FR? [Traceability]
47	
48	## Notes
49	
50	- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
51	- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
52	- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
53	- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
54	- Add comments or findings inline.
55	- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.

**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Account Deletion & Data Lifecycle (LGPD / RNF05)

- [ ] CHK001 Is "every piece of data tied to it" (RNF05) enumerated as a concrete, exhaustive list of locally-held data categories (session, cached profile, entries, chat, other), rather than left to an open-ended "any other locally held user data" phrase? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019, §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK002 Does the spec specify whether vault/PIN and biometric-preference local storage are included in or excluded from the account-deletion data wipe, given they are a separate on-device concern from the account itself? [Gap, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the requirement for a second concurrent delete attempt (FR-022) scoped to "Apagar tudo" specifically, and does the spec confirm no other in-flight request (e.g., a profile save) is expected to block or race with an account-deletion request? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK004 Does the spec define the dialog's behavior if the session expires while the delete-confirmation dialog is already open and the user has not yet tapped "Apagar tudo" vs. after tapping it but before the response resolves? [Edge Case, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK005 Are the specific failure modes for `DELETE /account` (timeout, no connection, malformed response, expired session) each traceable to a distinct, non-overlapping user-facing outcome, or could two of them produce indistinguishable error text? [Consistency, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK006 Is "malformed response" for the delete call defined precisely enough (e.g., any non-success body) to be distinguished from "no response" so the retry-ability of each is unambiguous? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK007 Does SC-004 ("zero account deletions occur without explicit confirmation") have a corresponding requirement covering accidental dismissal (tap-outside, back-gesture, OS back button) as equivalent to "Cancelar", not merely the two button taps? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-021, §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the irreversibility claim ("no way to undo it afterward") paired with a requirement stating there is no grace period, soft-delete, or recovery window on the backend side that the spec needs to account for? [Assumption, Spec User Story 2]

## Dashboard Aggregation & Narrative

- [ ] CHK009 Is the "roughly-equal time slices" bucketing rule (Assumptions) precise enough to be independently reproduced — i.e., does it specify how a non-evenly-divisible date range's remainder days are distributed among the ten bars? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK010 Does the spec define expected behavior when the account's full date range is shorter than ten days (e.g., 3 days of history across >1 entries), beyond "naturally produces a chart with some empty bars"? [Edge Case, Spec Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the boundary between the "exactly one entry" state (FR-004) and the "two or more entries" state (FR-005) specified in terms of the aggregate's entry count rather than UI appearance, so it cannot be misread as applying to bucket count instead? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK012 Are all distinct dashboard states (empty, single-entry, multi-entry/narrative-pending, multi-entry/narrative-shown, narrative-unavailable, aggregate-error) individually named/identifiable so no two can be confused with each other in an implementation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003–FR-007]
- [ ] CHK013 Does the spec address what the chart area shows while the aggregate request is still in flight (a loading state), or is this left undefined between "nothing yet" and the first of the enumerated states? [Gap, Coverage]
- [ ] CHK014 Is retry behavior specified for the aggregate-error state (FR-007 says "with a way to retry") — e.g., does retrying re-request both the aggregate and, if it succeeds, the narrative, or only the aggregate? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK015 Does the spec distinguish, for narrative failures, between a narrative that fails outright and one that times out, or are both intentionally treated identically under "narrativa indisponível" with no behavioral difference? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the requirement that the dashboard "MUST be recomputed from a fresh backend call every time Settings is opened" (FR-008) explicit about whether "opened" includes returning to Settings via back-navigation from a sub-screen, or only a fresh app-level navigation to it? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008]

## Profile, Biometric Toggle & Sign-Out

- [ ] CHK017 Is there a requirement guarding against a second concurrent name-save or biometric-toggle request analogous to FR-022's guard on "Sair"/"Apagar tudo", or is this double-submission case intentionally left uncovered for lower-risk actions? [Gap, Consistency, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK018 Is the display name's valid character set specified beyond a length bound (1–80 characters) — e.g., are whitespace-only names, emoji, or leading/trailing whitespace addressed? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK019 Does the spec define how the initials avatar is derived from a display name that has only one word, non-Latin characters, or is empty/default, so the avatar's content is unambiguous for every name state the spec allows? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK020 Is "the app's authentication entry point" (used identically by FR-016 and FR-019) defined with enough precision in the spec itself, or does it depend entirely on an external assumption resolved outside this spec's own requirements? [Traceability, Spec Assumptions, §FR-016, §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK021 Does the spec specify what the biometric toggle displays while its own save request is in flight (already-toggled optimistically vs. a pending/disabled state), distinct from the final success or revert-on-failure states in FR-013/FR-014? [Gap, Coverage]

## Cross-Cutting Consistency & Traceability

- [ ] CHK022 Are the generic failure phrases "timeout, no connection, malformed response" used across FR-007/FR-012/FR-014/FR-020 intended to cover every one of the backend's documented error codes (including rate-limiting), or could a code outside that phrase's literal scope produce an undefined outcome? [Completeness, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007, §FR-012, §FR-014, §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK023 Is the relationship between this spec's generic "existing expired-session handling... takes over exactly as it does elsewhere" (Edge Cases) and each individual FR's own failure-handling language made explicit, so a reader can tell session-expiry is an exception to FR-level retry/error requirements rather than a case those FRs also separately need to handle? [Consistency, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK024 Do FR-016 (sign-out) and FR-019 (account deletion) each unambiguously state which locally held data categories they clear, such that their difference (entries/chat cache cleared only on deletion) is a requirement a reader can derive from the spec text alone, not just inferred from the two being adjacent? [Clarity, Consistency, Spec §FR-016, §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK025 Are success criteria SC-001 through SC-006 each traceable to at least one specific functional requirement and acceptance scenario, with no measurable outcome left floating without a corresponding testable FR? [Traceability]

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.

- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.

# Tasks: P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/011-settings-dashboard/`
**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md (all present)

**Tests**: Not explicitly requested in spec.md beyond the constitutional RNF07 (≥80% domain coverage) and
RNF09 (full `Either`/scenario-table coverage) gates, which this project's every prior unit has satisfied with
real `flutter_test`/`bloc_test`/`mocktail` tests (not skipped). Test tasks are therefore included, scoped
exactly to what research.md/contracts/*.md's own scenario tables enumerate — no broader test suite than that.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story (US1 = dashboard, US2 = account deletion, US3 =
profile/biometric/sign-out) per spec.md's own priority order (US1 = P1, US2 = P1, US3 = P2). Foundational
work shared by all three stories (entities, the two existing-feature extensions, DI, tokens) is Phase 2.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependencies)
- **[Story]**: US1 (dashboard), US2 (account deletion), US3 (profile/biometric/sign-out)
- Every file path is exact; every entity/field constraint is quoted from data-model.md/contracts/*.md verbatim
  where one exists.

## Path Conventions

Single Flutter mobile project. New feature folder: `lib/features/settings/{domain,data,presentation}/`.
Tests mirror under `test/features/settings/` and `test/features/{auth,entries,chat,home}/` for the three
extended-in-place files, following this repo's existing `test/features/<feature>/<layer>/...` convention.

---

## Phase 1: Setup

No new dependencies, no new project scaffolding beyond the feature folder structure itself (plan.md Technical
Context: "No primary dependencies added"). This phase only creates the directory skeleton; no file content.

- [ ] T001 Create the empty `lib/features/settings/domain/entities/`, `lib/features/settings/domain/repositories/`,
  `lib/features/settings/domain/usecases/`, `lib/features/settings/data/`,
  `lib/features/settings/presentation/bloc/`, `lib/features/settings/presentation/widgets/` directories
  (`lib/features/settings/presentation/pages/` already exists, holding `settings_placeholder_page.dart`)

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: Domain entities, design tokens, and the three existing-feature extensions (`auth`, `entries`,
`chat`) that every user story's implementation phase depends on, plus DI wiring for everything not already
registered. **⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story phase can be completed until this phase is done — `SettingsBloc`
(built across all three story phases) depends on every repository/usecase interface defined here.

### Design tokens

- [ ] T002 [P] Add 5 new `DesignTokens` values to `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (research.md R14,
  data-model.md): `static const double sizeAvatarSettings = 52;` (prototype-extract.md §6, "52px in
  Configurações"), `static const double sizeChartBarMaxHeight = 120;`, `static const double
  sizeChartBarWidth = 20;`, `static const double sizeChartBarGap = 6;` (Sizes section), and `static const
  Color colorChartPlaceholder = Color(0xFFE1DACB);` (Colors section — same hex as existing `colorBorder`,

- [ ] T003 [P] Create `DashboardSourceCounts` (`{manual, audio, photo, chat}`, each `int`, each "≥ 0"
  data-model.md), `AggregateBucket` (`{date: DateTime, count: int, sources: DashboardSourceCounts}` — "Parsed
  from the backend's `YYYY-MM-DD` string, date-only (no time component kept)", "count ≥ 0"), and
  `DashboardTotals` (`{count: int, sources: DashboardSourceCounts}`) in
  `lib/features/settings/domain/entities/dashboard_aggregate.dart`, each `Equatable`
- [ ] T004 [P] Create `DashboardAggregate` (`{buckets: List<AggregateBucket>, totals: DashboardTotals}`,
  `Equatable`) with the pure method `List<int> tenBars({DateTime? today})` in
  `lib/features/settings/domain/entities/dashboard_aggregate.dart`, implementing the exact algorithm from
  research.md R2: if `buckets.isEmpty` return `List.filled(10, 0)`; else compute `start` as the earliest
  bucket date, `totalDaySpan = (today ?? DateTime.now()).difference(start).inDays`; if `totalDaySpan == 0`,
  put the full summed count in `bars[9]`; otherwise for each bucket compute `index = (daysSinceStart * 10) ~/
  (totalDaySpan + 1)` clamped to `[0, 9]` and accumulate `count` into `bars[index]`

### Existing-feature extensions (`auth`, `entries`, `chat`) — additive methods only

  `lib/features/auth/domain/repositories/auth_repository.dart`
- [ ] T012 Add `Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> logout()` to `AuthRemoteDataSource`
  (`lib/features/auth/data/auth_remote_data_source.dart`), calling `auth-logout` (`POST /auth/logout`,

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies — can start immediately.
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup. Blocks all three user story phases — every story's
  `SettingsBloc` work depends on the entities/repository interfaces/usecase/extensions defined here.
- **User Story 1 (Phase 3)**: Depends on Phase 2. Also creates the shared `settings_event.dart`/
  `settings_state.dart`/`settings_bloc.dart`/`settings_page.dart` files that Phases 4 and 5 extend in place.
- **User Story 2 (Phase 4)**: Depends on Phase 2 and on Phase 3's creation of `settings_bloc.dart`/
  `settings_page.dart` (it extends those files rather than creating new ones) — cannot start in true
  parallel with Phase 3 on those shared files, though its own new files (T038, T039, T042) can be built
  ahead of time.
- **User Story 3 (Phase 5)**: Same shared-file dependency on Phase 3 as Phase 4; independent of Phase 4's
  own new files otherwise.
- **Polish (Phase 6)**: Depends on Phases 3, 4, and 5 all being complete.

### User Story Dependencies

- **US1**: No dependency on US2/US3's own logic — the dashboard section is fully self-contained once Phase
  2 is done.
- **US2**: No functional dependency on US1 beyond sharing `settings_bloc.dart`/`settings_page.dart` as files
  (the delete flow reads no dashboard state).
- **US3**: No functional dependency on US1/US2 beyond the same shared files; profile/biometric/sign-out
  logic is independent of both.

### Within Each User Story

- Tests before implementation where both exist for the same unit of work.
- Data sources before repository impls; repository impls before bloc handlers; bloc handlers before widgets
  that dispatch their events; widgets before the page that assembles them; DI registration last (needs the
  concrete classes to exist).

### Parallel Opportunities

- All Phase 2 entity tasks (T003–T006) are `[P]` — different files, no interdependency beyond T004 extending
  the same file T003 creates (sequential within that one file, parallel with T005/T006).
- All Phase 2 repository-interface tasks (T007–T009) are `[P]`.
- The three existing-feature extension tracks (`auth`: T011→T012→T013; `entries`: T014/T015→T016; `chat`:
  T017/T018→T019) are mutually `[P]` as tracks, sequential within each track.
- T020/T021 (foundational tests) are `[P]`.
- Within US1: T023/T024 (tests, same file but independent scenario groups — write together), T025 alongside
  T027/T028 are `[P]`; T030/T031/T032 (three independent widget files) are `[P]`.
- Within US2: T036/T037 are `[P]`; T042 is `[P]` with the bloc-handler work (T041).
- Within US3: T045/T046/T047 are `[P]`; T049/T050 are `[P]`; T055/T056 are `[P]`.

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)

1. Complete Phase 1: Setup.
2. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (CRITICAL — blocks everything).
3. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1.
4. **STOP and VALIDATE**: Run quickstart.md Story 1's five numbered checks against accounts A–D.
5. Settings now shows a correct, real dashboard in place of the placeholder — a demoable increment even
   before account deletion or profile editing exist.

### Incremental Delivery

1. Setup + Foundational → shared foundation ready.
2. Add User Story 1 → validate independently → the dashboard is live (MVP).
3. Add User Story 2 → validate independently → "Apagar conta" is live, RNF05's compliance gate satisfied.
4. Add User Story 3 → validate independently → profile editing, biometrics, and "Sair" complete the screen.
5. Phase 6 polish (placeholder deletion, architecture re-checks, coverage, full quickstart) closes the unit.

### Parallel Team Strategy

With multiple developers, once Phase 2 is done: one developer takes US1 (and creates the shared bloc/page
files), while a second prepares US2's and a third prepares US3's own new files (data sources, repository
impls, widgets) ahead of time — the only serialization point is each one's final bloc-handler/page-wiring
task (T041/T043, T054/T057), which must land after Phase 3's T029/T033 exist.

## Summary

The Settings screen (`AppRoutes.settings`, currently `SettingsPlaceholderPage`) becomes a real, four-concern
screen backed by one screen-scoped `SettingsBloc`: (1) an evolution dashboard — `GET /dashboard/aggregate` and
`GET /dashboard/narrative` as two independent calls, the aggregate's ten-bar chart built by a new pure
derivation (`DashboardAggregate.tenBars()`, research.md R2) and rendered with plain `Container`-based bars
(no new charting dependency, research.md R3); (2) an editable profile header (52px initials avatar, inline
pencil-to-check name editing via `PATCH /account/settings`, read-only email) backed by a new, narrow
`AccountProfileRepository` whose confirmed writes persist into a new `AccountProfileLocalCache`
(`features/settings/data/`, Keychain-backed) — the one local mirror this unit adds, since no earlier unit
ever wrote `displayName`; (3) a biometrics toggle that is hidden entirely on a device with no usable
capability and otherwise reuses RF03's own `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`/`VaultRepository` as-is behind a
new, settings-owned, await-then-revert usecase (research.md R6) rather than RF03's deliberately
fire-and-forget one; (4) "Sair" (extends the existing `AuthRepository` with one new method, `logout()`) and
"Apagar conta" (a new `AccountDeletionRepository`, `DELETE /account`), both ending in the same
clear-local-state-and-navigate sequence spec.md's own Assumptions resolve to the existing vault/login routes
(research.md R10) — deletion alone additionally wipes `EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache` (both extended in
place with a new `clear()` method) since "any other locally held user data" (FR-019) is a strictly wider
clear than logout's own FR-016 wording. `app_drawer.dart` is extended in place to read the same cached display
name (research.md R13), and `SettingsPage` becomes `RouteAware` on the already-existing `chatRouteObserver` so
re-authenticating mid-screen re-requests fresh data rather than only preserving stale state (research.md R15).

contract ever disagree, the contract prevails (Constitution Principle I).

## Domain entities (`lib/features/settings/domain/entities/`)

### `AggregateBucket`
| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `date` | `DateTime` | Parsed from the backend's `YYYY-MM-DD` string, date-only (no time component kept). |
| `count` | `int` | ≥ 0. |
| `sources` | `DashboardSourceCounts` | `{manual, audio, photo, chat}`, each `int` ≥ 0 — carried for completeness; this unit's chart only ever renders `count` (no per-source stacking/legend in scope). |

### `DashboardTotals`
`{count: int, sources: DashboardSourceCounts}` — the account-wide total for the requested period.

`{buckets: List<AggregateBucket>, totals: DashboardTotals}`. One pure extension method:
- `List<int> tenBars({DateTime? today})` → `research.md R2`'s `tenBars` function, `today` defaulting to
  `DateTime.now()` but overridable for deterministic tests.

### `DashboardNarrative`
`{text: String, generatedAt: DateTime}` — `generatedAt` is parsed but never displayed (spec.md: the
narrative's own content/quality is out of scope); kept only because the response always carries it and
dropping a required field silently would be a worse modeling choice than keeping it unused.

### `AccountProfile`
| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `displayName` | `String` | 1–80 chars once set; the screen's single source of truth for both the name field and avatar initials. |
| `email` | `String` | Read-only in this unit (FR-009); sourced from `SessionRepository`'s already-resolved `Account.email`, never from a Settings-owned call. |

Static/instance helpers (research.md R13):
- `static String defaultDisplayNameFromEmail(String email)` — splits the email's local part on `._-`,
  title-cases each word, joins with a space (`"wagner.duarte@x.com"` → `"Wagner Duarte"`); `email` itself if

1	# Research: P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
2	
3	Phase 0 output. Each item is a technical-judgment decision this plan must make beyond what spec.md's own FRs/
4	Clarifications/Assumptions already resolve (Constitution Principle I: "where these documents are silent,
5	implementers MUST make a reasonable technical decision rather than block on clarification"). None of these
6	reopen a resolved Clarification; each builds directly on spec.md's own wording.
7	
8	## R1 — Dashboard data flow is two independent repository calls, gated by `totals.count`
9	
10	`DashboardRepository.fetchAggregate()` and `fetchNarrative()` are two separate methods, called separately by
11	`SettingsBloc`, never composed into one. The aggregate call always fires on `SettingsOpened`/retry (FR-001,
12	FR-008). The narrative call fires only after the aggregate succeeds **and** `aggregate.totals.count >= 2`
13	(FR-003/FR-004/FR-005) — the bloc inspects the already-resolved aggregate's own total, never a second network
14	round-trip to "find out" the count. Both calls send the single fixed query parameter `period=all` (spec.md
15	Assumption "Dashboard period") — no period parameter is ever user-controlled in this unit.
16	
17	## R2 — Ten-bar bucketing is a pure, total function over `(buckets, today)`
18	
19	Spec.md's Clarification/Assumption fixes the algorithm in words ("divide the account's full date range — date
20	of the first entry through today — into ten roughly-equal time slices and sum the per-date counts falling
21	within each slice"); this unit only has to fix the exact integer arithmetic so the function is deterministic
22	and testable:
23	
24	```
25	List<int> tenBars(List<AggregateBucket> buckets, DateTime today) {
26	  if (buckets.isEmpty) return List.filled(10, 0);
27	  final start = buckets.map((b) => b.date).reduce((a, b) => a.isBefore(b) ? a : b);
28	  final totalDaySpan = today.difference(start).inDays; // >= 0; both date-only (UTC midnight)
29	  final bars = List.filled(10, 0);
30	  if (totalDaySpan == 0) {
31	    // Every entry happened "today" relative to the account's own first entry
32	    // (e.g. 2 entries created minutes apart) — a single-day range cannot be
33	    // divided into 10 meaningful slices, so the whole total lands in the
34	    // last bar rather than every bar collapsing onto index 0.
35	    bars[9] = buckets.fold(0, (sum, b) => sum + b.count);
36	    return bars;
37	  }
38	  for (final bucket in buckets) {
39	    final daysSinceStart = bucket.date.difference(start).inDays;
40	    final index = (daysSinceStart * 10) ~/ (totalDaySpan + 1);
41	    bars[index.clamp(0, 9)] += bucket.count;
42	  }
43	  return bars;
44	}
45	```
46	`totalDaySpan + 1` (not `totalDaySpan`) is the slice divisor so the very last day (`daysSinceStart ==
47	totalDaySpan`) still lands inside bar index 9, not spilling past it. This function is pure (no `DateTime.now()`
48	inside it — the caller passes `today`), lives in `domain/`, and is the one piece of this unit's logic RNF07
49	most needs to hit ≥80% on, mirroring `DateRangeFilter`/`SyncBadgeState`'s existing pure-derivation shape.
50	
51	## R3 — No new charting dependency
52	
53	The chart is always exactly 10 bars with no interaction (no tooltip, no zoom, no legend) — a `Row` of 10
54	`Container`s whose heights are `count / maxBarCount * DesignTokens.sizeChartBarMaxHeight` (clamped to a
55	minimum visible sliver for a non-zero, sub-pixel bar) already renders this losslessly with widgets the app
56	already depends on. Adding `fl_chart`/`syncfusion_flutter_charts`/etc. for 10 static bars would be the first
57	charting dependency in the app for a shape plain `Flutter` already draws — rejected (Complexity Tracking).
58	Principle II's "chart package" being a free/open choice means "free to add one if needed," not "must add one."
59	
60	## R4 — `SettingsState` is one flat composite state, not a sealed per-mode hierarchy
61	
62	Unlike `VaultBloc` (a strictly sequential state machine — PIN setup, then biometric prompt, then unlock) or
63	`ExportBloc` (one sheet, one job, mutually exclusive terminal states), Settings' four concerns — dashboard,
64	narrative, profile/name-edit, biometric toggle, sign-out, account-deletion — load and update **independently**
65	of one another on the same screen at the same time (e.g. the name can be mid-edit while the dashboard is still
66	loading). `SettingsState` is therefore one `Equatable` class with a field per concern and a `copyWith` using
67	the same `_unset` sentinel pattern `RecordsLoaded` already establishes for nullable fields that must be
68	explicitly clearable — the same shape, scaled to more independent regions, not a new pattern.
69	
70	## R5 — Display-name caching: new, settings-owned local cache; biometric state: no new cache at all
71	
72	Spec.md's "Account Profile" Key Entity requires treating "the most recent successful write... as the locally
73	held source of truth," including biometricEnabled, "defaulting sensibly... for an account that has never had
74	a successful write." Splitting this per field is simpler and more correct than a single shared cache:
75	
76	- **`displayName`** has no on-device mirror anywhere else in the app — RF03 never writes it. A new
77	  `AccountProfileLocalCache` (`features/settings/data/`, Keychain-backed via `flutter_secure_storage`, same
78	  pattern as `VaultSecureStorage`/`EntriesLocalCache`) persists only the name this unit's own successful
79	  `PATCH` last confirmed. `AccountProfile.defaultDisplayNameFromEmail(email)` (see R13) supplies the sensible
80	  default when the cache is empty.
81	- **`biometricEnabled`** already has an authoritative, always-correct on-device mirror:
82	  `VaultRepository.isBiometricPreferenceEnabled()` (`VaultSecureStorage`), written synchronously during RF03's
83	  first-time setup regardless of whether that setup's own backend write succeeded (RF03 FR-014, local-first).
84	  Reading the toggle's initial state from there is *more* correct than inventing a second, settings-owned
85	  cache that RF03's write path would have to be taught to also populate — it is already "the most recent
86	  successful write" in the sense that matters (what the device itself currently enforces). No vault file needs
87	  to change for this unit to read it.
88	
89	## R6 — Settings' own biometric-toggle write path: await + revert, reusing RF03's repository as-is
90	
91	FR-014 ("the toggle MUST revert... rather than appearing to succeed") is the opposite contract from RF03's
92	existing `SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase` (`vault/domain/usecases/`), which is deliberately fire-and-forget
93	("always completes regardless of outcome" — RF03 research.md R6, first-time setup must never block on the
94	network). Rather than changing that usecase's contract (and risking RF03's own already-shipped behavior), this
95	unit adds a new, settings-owned usecase, `SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase`
96	(`features/settings/domain/usecases/`), that:
97	1. calls `BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save(enabled)` (vault's existing, single-field repository — reused
98	   verbatim, not re-implemented — "continuing the account-settings read/write path RF03 already established
99	   for this same flag," FR-013's own wording) and *awaits* the `Either`;
100	2. on `Right`: calls `VaultRepository.setBiometricPreferenceLocally(enabled)` so the device's own unlock gate
101	   and Settings' displayed value move together;
102	3. on `Left`: returns the failure untouched — the local mirror is never written, so a later app relock still
103	   gates on the last-confirmed value, and `SettingsBloc` reverts the toggle's optimistic UI flip.
104	
105	`BiometricsPreferenceRepository`/`BiometricsPreferenceRemoteDataSource` (vault/) are unmodified; this is a new
106	caller, not a new implementation.
107	
108	## R7 — Display-name write path: new, narrow `AccountProfileRepository`
109	
110	Mirrors `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`'s own documented reasoning ("deliberately narrow... rather than a
111	general-purpose account-settings repository"). A new `AccountSettingsRemoteDataSource.updateDisplayName()`
112	(`features/settings/data/`) sends `PATCH account-settings-update` with `{"displayName": ...}` only (never
113	`persona`, FR-015). `AccountProfileRepositoryImpl.updateDisplayName()` persists the confirmed name into
114	`AccountProfileLocalCache` before returning `Right` (FR-010, SC-005), and never touches `biometricEnabled` or
115	`persona` — a client-side-only `AccountProfile` validation (1–80 chars, FR-011) runs in the bloc before any
116	repository call, so an invalid name never reaches the network.
117	
118	## R8 — Logout extends the existing `auth/` feature; account deletion is new, inside `settings/`
119	
120	`POST /auth/logout` (`auth-logout`) is an auth-domain concern indistinguishable in shape from
121	`auth-signup`/`auth-login`, already owned by `AuthRepository`/`AuthRemoteDataSource`/`AuthRepositoryImpl`
122	(`features/auth/`) — this unit adds one method, `logout()`, to all three, the same "extend an earlier unit's
123	file in place" precedent RF05 already set on `records_page.dart`. `DELETE /account` (`account-delete`) is new
124	and squarely RF09/RNF05-owned, so it gets its own repository inside `features/settings/`
125	(`AccountDeletionRepository`/`AccountDeletionRemoteDataSource`/`AccountDeletionRepositoryImpl`), sending the
126	backend-required `{"confirmation": "DELETE"}` body the user never types (FR-018).
127	
128	## R9 — What gets cleared locally: logout is narrower than account deletion, by FR text
129

# Research: P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard

Phase 0 output. Each item is a technical-judgment decision this plan must make beyond what spec.md's own FRs/
Clarifications/Assumptions already resolve (Constitution Principle I: "where these documents are silent,
implementers MUST make a reasonable technical decision rather than block on clarification"). None of these
reopen a resolved Clarification; each builds directly on spec.md's own wording.

## R1 — Dashboard data flow is two independent repository calls, gated by `totals.count`

`DashboardRepository.fetchAggregate()` and `fetchNarrative()` are two separate methods, called separately by
`SettingsBloc`, never composed into one. The aggregate call always fires on `SettingsOpened`/retry (FR-001,
FR-008). The narrative call fires only after the aggregate succeeds **and** `aggregate.totals.count >= 2`
(FR-003/FR-004/FR-005) — the bloc inspects the already-resolved aggregate's own total, never a second network
round-trip to "find out" the count. Both calls send the single fixed query parameter `period=all` (spec.md
Assumption "Dashboard period") — no period parameter is ever user-controlled in this unit.

## R2 — Ten-bar bucketing is a pure, total function over `(buckets, today)`

Spec.md's Clarification/Assumption fixes the algorithm in words ("divide the account's full date range — date
of the first entry through today — into ten roughly-equal time slices and sum the per-date counts falling
within each slice"); this unit only has to fix the exact integer arithmetic so the function is deterministic
and testable:

```
List<int> tenBars(List<AggregateBucket> buckets, DateTime today) {
  if (buckets.isEmpty) return List.filled(10, 0);
  final start = buckets.map((b) => b.date).reduce((a, b) => a.isBefore(b) ? a : b);
  final totalDaySpan = today.difference(start).inDays; // >= 0; both date-only (UTC midnight)
  final bars = List.filled(10, 0);
  if (totalDaySpan == 0) {
    // Every entry happened "today" relative to the account's own first entry
    // (e.g. 2 entries created minutes apart) — a single-day range cannot be
    // divided into 10 meaningful slices, so the whole total lands in the
    // last bar rather than every bar collapsing onto index 0.
    bars[9] = buckets.fold(0, (sum, b) => sum + b.count);
    return bars;
  }
  for (final bucket in buckets) {
    final daysSinceStart = bucket.date.difference(start).inDays;
    final index = (daysSinceStart * 10) ~/ (totalDaySpan + 1);
    bars[index.clamp(0, 9)] += bucket.count;
  }
  return bars;
}
```
`totalDaySpan + 1` (not `totalDaySpan`) is the slice divisor so the very last day (`daysSinceStart ==
totalDaySpan`) still lands inside bar index 9, not spilling past it. This function is pure (no `DateTime.now()`
inside it — the caller passes `today`), lives in `domain/`, and is the one piece of this unit's logic RNF07
most needs to hit ≥80% on, mirroring `DateRangeFilter`/`SyncBadgeState`'s existing pure-derivation shape.

## R3 — No new charting dependency

The chart is always exactly 10 bars with no interaction (no tooltip, no zoom, no legend) — a `Row` of 10
`Container`s whose heights are `count / maxBarCount * DesignTokens.sizeChartBarMaxHeight` (clamped to a
minimum visible sliver for a non-zero, sub-pixel bar) already renders this losslessly with widgets the app
already depends on. Adding `fl_chart`/`syncfusion_flutter_charts`/etc. for 10 static bars would be the first
charting dependency in the app for a shape plain `Flutter` already draws — rejected (Complexity Tracking).
Principle II's "chart package" being a free/open choice means "free to add one if needed," not "must add one."

## R4 — `SettingsState` is one flat composite state, not a sealed per-mode hierarchy

Unlike `VaultBloc` (a strictly sequential state machine — PIN setup, then biometric prompt, then unlock) or
`ExportBloc` (one sheet, one job, mutually exclusive terminal states), Settings' four concerns — dashboard,
narrative, profile/name-edit, biometric toggle, sign-out, account-deletion — load and update **independently**
of one another on the same screen at the same time (e.g. the name can be mid-edit while the dashboard is still
loading). `SettingsState` is therefore one `Equatable` class with a field per concern and a `copyWith` using
the same `_unset` sentinel pattern `RecordsLoaded` already establishes for nullable fields that must be
explicitly clearable — the same shape, scaled to more independent regions, not a new pattern.

## R5 — Display-name caching: new, settings-owned local cache; biometric state: no new cache at all

Spec.md's "Account Profile" Key Entity requires treating "the most recent successful write... as the locally
held source of truth," including biometricEnabled, "defaulting sensibly... for an account that has never had
a successful write." Splitting this per field is simpler and more correct than a single shared cache:

- **`displayName`** has no on-device mirror anywhere else in the app — RF03 never writes it. A new
  `AccountProfileLocalCache` (`features/settings/data/`, Keychain-backed via `flutter_secure_storage`, same
  pattern as `VaultSecureStorage`/`EntriesLocalCache`) persists only the name this unit's own successful
  `PATCH` last confirmed. `AccountProfile.defaultDisplayNameFromEmail(email)` (see R13) supplies the sensible
  default when the cache is empty.
- **`biometricEnabled`** already has an authoritative, always-correct on-device mirror:
  `VaultRepository.isBiometricPreferenceEnabled()` (`VaultSecureStorage`), written synchronously during RF03's
  first-time setup regardless of whether that setup's own backend write succeeded (RF03 FR-014, local-first).
  Reading the toggle's initial state from there is *more* correct than inventing a second, settings-owned
  cache that RF03's write path would have to be taught to also populate — it is already "the most recent
  successful write" in the sense that matters (what the device itself currently enforces). No vault file needs
  to change for this unit to read it.

## R6 — Settings' own biometric-toggle write path: await + revert, reusing RF03's repository as-is

FR-014 ("the toggle MUST revert... rather than appearing to succeed") is the opposite contract from RF03's
existing `SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase` (`vault/domain/usecases/`), which is deliberately fire-and-forget
("always completes regardless of outcome" — RF03 research.md R6, first-time setup must never block on the
network). Rather than changing that usecase's contract (and risking RF03's own already-shipped behavior), this
unit adds a new, settings-owned usecase, `SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase`
(`features/settings/domain/usecases/`), that:
1. calls `BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save(enabled)` (vault's existing, single-field repository — reused

2. on `Right`: calls `VaultRepository.setBiometricPreferenceLocally(enabled)` so the device's own unlock gate
   and Settings' displayed value move together;
3. on `Left`: returns the failure untouched — the local mirror is never written, so a later app relock still
   gates on the last-confirmed value, and `SettingsBloc` reverts the toggle's optimistic UI flip.

caller, not a new implementation.

1	# Contract: `DashboardRepository`
2	
3	`features/settings/domain/repositories/dashboard_repository.dart`, implemented by
4	`DashboardRepositoryImpl` (`features/settings/data/`), backed by `DashboardRemoteDataSource` calling
5	`dashboard-aggregate-get` (`GET /dashboard/aggregate?period=all`) and `dashboard-narrative-get`
6	(`GET /dashboard/narrative?period=all`).
7	
8	```dart
9	abstract class DashboardRepository {
10	  Future<Either<Failure, DashboardAggregate>> fetchAggregate();
11	  Future<Either<Failure, DashboardNarrative>> fetchNarrative();
12	}
13	```
14	
15	## Parsing
16	
17	`fetchAggregate()` decodes `data.buckets[]` (`date`, `count`, `sources.{manual,audio,photo,chat}`) and
18	`data.totals` (`count`, `sources`) per `openapi.yaml`'s schema (both always present, even for a zero-entry

# Contract: `DashboardRepository`

`features/settings/domain/repositories/dashboard_repository.dart`, implemented by
`DashboardRepositoryImpl` (`features/settings/data/`), backed by `DashboardRemoteDataSource` calling
`dashboard-aggregate-get` (`GET /dashboard/aggregate?period=all`) and `dashboard-narrative-get`
(`GET /dashboard/narrative?period=all`).

```dart
abstract class DashboardRepository {
  Future<Either<Failure, DashboardAggregate>> fetchAggregate();
  Future<Either<Failure, DashboardNarrative>> fetchNarrative();
}
```

## Parsing

`fetchAggregate()` decodes `data.buckets[]` (`date`, `count`, `sources.{manual,audio,photo,chat}`) and
`data.totals` (`count`, `sources`) per `openapi.yaml`'s schema (both always present, even for a zero-entry
account — "always 200" per the contract's own summary line). `fetchNarrative()` decodes `data.text`/
`data.generatedAt`. A missing/mistyped required field on either call is a `ValidationFailure` (`TypeError`
caught, never thrown past this boundary — same pattern as `SessionRepositoryImpl._assembleFromCheckSession`).

## Retry-once-on-expiry

Both methods follow `EntriesRepositoryImpl._retryAfterSilentRefresh`'s exact shape: on `AuthExpiredFailure`,
call `SessionRepository.refresh()` once; on its own failure, return
`Left(AuthExpiredFailure(message: 'Session could not be renewed'))` (no second refresh attempt); on success,
retry the original call exactly once more and return whatever it resolves to.

## Scenario table (RNF09 — `fetchAggregate`/`fetchNarrative` are `GET`s, outside the write-endpoint tally,
but still fully `Either`-typed and tested)

| # | Scenario | Expected `Either` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 200, zero-entry account (`buckets: []`, `totals.count: 0`) | `Right(DashboardAggregate)` with an empty bucket list — never a `Left` |
| 2 | 200, well-formed non-empty payload | `Right(DashboardAggregate)` / `Right(DashboardNarrative)` |
| 3 | Dio timeout | `Left(NetworkTimeoutFailure)` |
| 4 | No connection (no response) | `Left(NetworkOfflineFailure)` |
| 5 | 200 with a malformed body (`buckets` not a list / `count` missing) | `Left(ValidationFailure)` |
| 6 | 401 `AUTH_EXPIRED`, silent refresh succeeds | retried call's own result (success path re-exercises #1/#2) |
| 7 | 401 `AUTH_EXPIRED`, silent refresh itself fails | `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)`, and `SettingsBloc.reauthRequired` fires |
| 8 | `dashboard-narrative-get` returns `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | `Left(AiGenerationTimeoutFailure)` — mapped by `ErrorMapper` unchanged, surfaced by `SettingsBloc` as the "narrativa indisponível" state (FR-006), never conflated with #1's empty-history copy |

## `DashboardAggregate.tenBars()` — see data-model.md / research.md R2

Exercised directly by a domain unit test (no repository/network involved) for: empty input (10 zeros), a
single bucket on "today" (all weight in bar 9), buckets spanning exactly 10 days (one bucket per bar,

29	PIN hash and biometrics-preference mirror are deliberately **not** touched (research.md R9/R10).

# Contract: Sign-out (`AuthRepository.logout()` extension) + shared post-action destination

## `AuthRepository.logout()` — extends an existing interface (research.md R8)

`features/auth/domain/repositories/auth_repository.dart` gains one method, implemented by
`AuthRepositoryImpl` via a new `AuthRemoteDataSource.logout()` calling `auth-logout` (`POST /auth/logout`,
`bearerAuth`, empty body):

```dart
Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> logout();
```

`auth-logout`'s own response is `{data: {ok: true}}`; this method returns `Right(unit)` on 200 regardless of
the `ok` value's content (unlike `account-delete`, a non-`true` `ok` here is not treated as a malformed
response worth blocking on — FR-016 already says the local session is cleared "regardless of whether that
call succeeds or fails"). `AuthRepositoryImpl.logout()` does **not** call `SecureTokenStorage`/
`SessionRepository.clear()` itself — that stays `SettingsBloc`'s job (below), so `AuthRepository` keeps its
existing shape (it has never owned session-clearing; `AuthRepositoryImpl._persistOnSuccess` only ever writes,
never deletes).

## `SettingsBloc`'s sign-out sequence (FR-016)

```
on SignOutRequested, if isSigningOut: ignore (FR-022)
set isSigningOut = true
await authRepository.logout()        // result intentionally discarded either way
await sessionRepository.clear()
await accountProfileRepository.clearCachedDisplayName()
destination = hasPinConfigured() ? vault : login   // research.md R10
emit SettingsState(..., signedOutDestination: destination)
```
Note the `logout()` call's `Either` is awaited (so the request actually completes before local state is
wiped — avoiding a race where the app's own token is already gone when the request tries to attach it) but
never branched on; both `Left` and `Right` fall through to the same unconditional clear-and-navigate sequence
this is the one place in this unit's bloc logic where a `Left` is deliberately not surfaced as an error, per
FR-016's own explicit wording.

## Scenario table

| # | Scenario | Local state after | Navigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `logout()` → `Right`, PIN configured | Session + cached name cleared | `AppRoutes.vault` |
| 2 | `logout()` → `Right`, no PIN configured (should not occur post-RF03, but not assumed impossible) | Session + cached name cleared | `AppRoutes.login` |
| 3 | `logout()` → `Left` (timeout/offline/`AUTH_EXPIRED`/malformed) | Session + cached name cleared regardless | Same as #1/#2 — failure never blocks the clear-and-leave sequence |
| 4 | A second `SignOutRequested` arrives while `isSigningOut == true` | No second `logout()` call (FR-022) | No second navigation |

`EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache` are **not** cleared on sign-out (research.md R9) — only
`AccountDeletionRepository`'s success path (contracts/account-deletion-repository.md) does that.

1	# Contract: Settings' biometric toggle (research.md R6) — a new caller, zero changes to `vault/`
2	
3	`SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase` (`features/settings/domain/usecases/`):
4	
5	```dart
6	class SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase {
7	  const SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase({
8	    required BiometricsPreferenceRepository biometricsPreferenceRepository, // vault/domain/, unmodified
9	    required VaultRepository vaultRepository,                               // vault/domain/, unmodified
10	  });
11	
12	  Future<Either<Failure, void>> call(bool enabled) async {
13	    final result = await _biometricsPreferenceRepository.save(enabled);
14	    return result.match(
15	      (failure) => Left(failure), // local mirror left untouched — next relock still gates on the old value
16	      (_) async {
17	        await _vaultRepository.setBiometricPreferenceLocally(enabled);
18	        return const Right(null);
19	      },
20	    );
21	  }
22	}
23	```
24	
25	## Reads for the toggle's initial state / visibility (`SettingsBloc`, on `SettingsOpened`)
26	
27	```dart
28	final capability = await vaultRepository.checkBiometricCapability();
29	final visible = capability == BiometricCapability.available;         // FR-013's "hidden entirely" rule
30	final enabled = visible ? await vaultRepository.isBiometricPreferenceEnabled() : false;
31	```
32	`noHardware`/`notEnrolled`/`osDisabled` all resolve to `visible = false` — the same "all non-`available`
33	outcomes are routed identically" reading `VaultBloc`'s own `BiometricAuthOutcome` handling already
34	establishes for its own enum (RF03, contracts/vault-repository.md).
35	
36	## Scenario table
37	
38	| # | Scenario | `SettingsBloc` reaction |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| 1 | `checkBiometricCapability() == available` | Toggle row shown, initial value from `isBiometricPreferenceEnabled()` |
41	| 2 | `noHardware` / `notEnrolled` / `osDisabled` | Toggle row omitted entirely from `SettingsState` (`biometricToggleVisible = false`) — no disabled/grayed row |
42	| 3 | User flips the toggle; `save()` → `Right` | UI already shows the flipped value optimistically (RNF01, <100ms); `VaultRepository`'s mirror updated to match — confirmed |
43	| 4 | User flips the toggle; `save()` → `Left` (timeout/offline/malformed) | UI reverts to the pre-flip value, `biometricFailureMessage` set, mirror left untouched (FR-014) |
44	| 5 | `save()` returns `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)` after a failed silent refresh | Same revert as #4, plus `reauthRequired` fires |
45	
46	This usecase is exercised with `mocktail` fakes of `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`/`VaultRepository` — no new
47	test doubles for `local_auth`/`flutter_secure_storage` are needed, since neither is touched directly here.

1	# Contract: `SettingsBloc`
2	
3	`features/settings/presentation/bloc/`. A `get_it` `registerFactory` (screen-scoped, same lifetime pattern as
4	`RecordsBloc`/`ExportBloc` — a fresh instance per `AppRoutes.settings` visit, never a singleton, since
5	FR-008/FR-023 require a fresh fetch on every open rather than a resumed prior state).
6	
7	## Dependencies
8	
9	`DashboardRepository`, `AccountProfileRepository`, `AccountDeletionRepository`, `AuthRepository`,
10	`SessionRepository`, `SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase`, `VaultRepository` — no `SessionBloc` import
11	(research.md R11 keeps that cross-bloc touch at the page, not the bloc, same as `RecordsBloc`).
12	
13	## Events
14	
15	| Event | Triggers |
16	|---|---|
17	| `SettingsOpened` | Dispatched once by the route builder (`app_router.dart`), mirroring `RecordsStarted`. Kicks off: aggregate fetch → (conditionally) narrative fetch; profile load (`SessionRepository`'s cached `Account.email` + `AccountProfileRepository.readCachedDisplayName()` or the email-derived default); biometric capability + current value. |
18	| `DashboardRetryRequested` | Re-runs the aggregate (and, if it then qualifies, narrative) fetch — FR-007's retry affordance. |
19	| `NameEditStarted` | `nameEditStatus → editing`, `nameDraft` seeded with the current `displayName`. |
20	| `NameDraftChanged(String value)` | Updates `nameDraft` only — no validation yet. |
21	| `NameEditCancelled` | `nameEditStatus → viewing`, `nameDraft` discarded. |
22	| `NameEditSubmitted` | Validates `nameDraft` first (FR-011); on failure, sets `nameEditFailureMessage`, stays `editing`, **no repository call**. On pass, calls `AccountProfileRepository.updateDisplayName`; on `Right`, `displayName` updates and `nameEditStatus → viewing`; on `Left`, stays `editing` with `nameDraft` intact and a retryable message (FR-012). |
23	| `BiometricToggleChanged(bool value)` | Optimistically flips `biometricEnabled` (RNF01), calls `SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase`; reverts + message on `Left` (contracts/biometric-preference-settings-extension.md). |
24	| `SignOutRequested` | contracts/account-session-actions.md. |
25	| `DeleteAccountDialogOpened` / `DeleteAccountDialogCancelled` | Presentation-only — toggles `deleteDialogOpen`; cancel makes **no** backend call (FR-021). |
26	| `DeleteAccountConfirmed` | contracts/account-deletion-repository.md. |
27	
28	## `reauthRequired` (research.md R11)
29	
30	```dart
31	final _reauthController = StreamController<void>.broadcast();
32	Stream<void> get reauthRequired => _reauthController.stream;
33	```
34	Fired from inside any repository-call handler whenever the result is `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)` *after* that
35	repository's own single silent-refresh retry has already been exhausted (never for the first attempt, which
36	retries silently without surfacing anything) — same trigger condition `RecordsBloc`/`ChatSessionsBloc` already
37	use for their own `reauthRequired` streams. `close()` overridden to also close `_reauthController`, mirroring
38	`RecordsBloc`.
39	
40	## `SettingsPage` wiring (`features/settings/presentation/pages/settings_page.dart`)
41	
42	```dart
43	late final StreamSubscription<void> _reauthSubscription;
44	
45	@override
46	void initState() {
47	  super.initState();
48	  _reauthSubscription = context.read<SettingsBloc>().reauthRequired.listen((_) {
49	    if (!mounted) return;
50	    context.read<SessionBloc>().add(const AuthExpiredDetected());
51	  });
52	}
53	```
54	A `BlocListener<SettingsBloc, SettingsState>` with `listenWhen` on `signedOutDestination`/
55	`accountDeletedDestination` becoming non-null performs the `context.go()` (research.md R10); a second
56	`BlocListener` (or the same one) shows the delete-confirmation `AlertDialog` while `deleteDialogOpen == true`,
57	closing it automatically on a successful deletion (the destination-change listener fires in the same frame).
58	
59	## Session-expiry mid-screen (spec.md Edge Cases; research.md R15)
60	
61	The existing `main.dart`-level `BlocListener<SessionBloc>` raises the overlay exactly as it does for every
62	other screen — no change there. Re-authenticating does **not** rebuild `SettingsPage`/`SettingsBloc` (the
63	reauth `LoginSignupPage` is pushed on top of, then popped back to, the same still-mounted `SettingsPage` —
64	`showSessionExpiredOverlay`'s own existing mechanism); instead, `SettingsPage`'s `State` is `RouteAware`,
65	subscribed to the already-existing `chatRouteObserver` (`app_router.dart`):
66	
67	```dart
68	@override
69	void didChangeDependencies() {
70	  super.didChangeDependencies();
71	  chatRouteObserver.subscribe(this, ModalRoute.of(context)! as PageRoute<void>);
72	}
73	
74	@override
75	void dispose() {
76	  chatRouteObserver.unsubscribe(this);
77	  super.dispose();
78	}
79	
80	@override
81	void didPopNext() => context.read<SettingsBloc>().add(const SettingsOpened());
82	```
83	
84	So the dashboard, profile, and biometric toggle are "reasonably re-requested" the moment the reauth page above
85	Settings is popped — matching spec.md's own wording, which is deliberately stronger here than Records'/Chat's
86	"preserve state, don't necessarily refetch" handling of the same overlay. An in-progress name edit
87	(`nameEditStatus == editing`, `nameDraft` holding unsaved text) is **not** reset by this `SettingsOpened`
88	re-dispatch — the handler only refills `dashboardStatus`/`aggregate`/`narrativeStatus`/`biometricEnabled`/
89	`displayName` (the latter only when not currently being edited), leaving `nameEditStatus`/`nameDraft` alone so
90	the user's in-progress text survives re-authentication too ("any in-progress edit... not silently lost").

# Contract: `AppDrawer`'s display name (research.md R13) — extended in place, no behavior regression

`lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/app_drawer.dart` currently derives both the shown name and the
avatar's initials straight from the email (`_displayNameFromEmail`/`_initialsFromEmail`/`_emailNameWords`),
with a comment naming this unit as the one that wires in a real name. This unit:

1. Deletes `_displayNameFromEmail`/`_initialsFromEmail`/`_emailNameWords` from `app_drawer.dart`.
2. Adds `AccountProfile.defaultDisplayNameFromEmail`/`.initials` (data-model.md) to
   `features/settings/domain/entities/account_profile.dart`, carrying the exact same splitting/title-casing
   behavior forward byte-for-byte (same regex, same join) — not a rewrite, a relocation.
3. `_AppDrawerState` resolves its displayed name as:
   ```dart
   final cached = await getIt<AccountProfileRepository>().readCachedDisplayName();
   final email = await getIt<SecureTokenStorage>().readAccountEmail();
   final displayName = cached ?? (email == null ? null : AccountProfile.defaultDisplayNameFromEmail(email));
   ```
   combined into one `Future<({String? displayName, String? email})>` (or two sequential `FutureBuilder`s —
   implementation detail left to tasks.md) so both pieces resolve before first paint, same as today's single
   `_accountEmail` future. The drawer depends on `AccountProfileRepository` (`settings/domain/`), not on
   `AccountProfileLocalCache` directly — a presentation file reaching into another feature's `data/` class
   directly would be a new, unprecedented cross-feature import shape; going through the domain-layer
   repository interface (already registered as a `get_it` lazy singleton for `SettingsBloc`'s own use) is the
   same "presentation depends on a domain interface, resolved via `get_it`" shape every other cross-feature
   touch in this app already uses.
4. The avatar's `Text` child becomes `AccountProfile(displayName: displayName ?? '?', email: ...).initials`
   instead of the deleted `_initialsFromEmail(email)` call.

## Why this is safe to do here, not deferred

`AccountProfileLocalCache` is a new class this unit already creates (data-model.md); reading it from
`app_drawer.dart` is a presentation→data-layer-via-cache read no different in kind from `SecureTokenStorage`'s
own existing use in the same file — no new architectural seam, just one more secure-storage key read
alongside the one already there. Skipping this step would leave the drawer showing the stand-in email-derived
name forever even after a user successfully renames themselves in Settings — a visible inconsistency between
two screens showing what is supposed to be the same identity, directly contradicted by the comment this unit
is explicitly resolving.

## Test impact

`test/features/home/presentation/` (if any widget test already pumps `AppDrawer` against a fixed email) gains
one more stubbed dependency (`AccountProfileLocalCache.readDisplayName() → null`) to keep its existing
assertions about the email-derived fallback passing unchanged; no existing assertion's *expected value*
changes, since `null` cached ⇒ identical output to today's always-derive-from-email behavior.

3	import 'package:cerne/features/entries/domain/entities/entry.dart';
4	import 'package:flutter_secure_storage/flutter_secure_storage.dart';
5	
6	/// On-device, cross-restart persistence for the entries the user has
7	/// already seen (the PRD's "local read cache" — requirements.md line 50/125:
8	/// results from it stay visible offline and reconcile with the server on
9	/// reconnect, with no duplicates). Keychain-backed, same pattern as
10	/// `VaultSecureStorage` — journal content is personal data, so it stays
11	/// encrypted at rest like the PIN it already sits behind.
12	///
13	/// Distinct from `EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s in-memory `cachedEntries`: that
14	/// field only ever held optimistic just-created entries for this process's
15	/// lifetime (research.md R8, 003-multimodal-capture). This class is what
16	/// makes that same list survive an app restart, which is what a cold open
17	/// on an already-offline device needs (closing snapshot at unit completion
18	/// did not cover this path — see Meus Registros intervention report).
19	class EntriesLocalCache {
20	  EntriesLocalCache({FlutterSecureStorage? storage})
21	    : _storage = storage ?? const FlutterSecureStorage();
22	
23	  final FlutterSecureStorage _storage;
24	
25	  static const _key = 'entriesLocalCache';
26	
27	  Future<List<Entry>> readAll() async {
28	    final raw = await _storage.read(key: _key);
29	    if (raw == null) return const [];
30	    try {
31	      final decoded = jsonDecode(raw) as List<dynamic>;
32	      return decoded.map((e) => _fromJson(e as Map<String, dynamic>)).toList();
33	    } on FormatException {
34	      return const [];
35	    } on TypeError {
36	      return const [];
37	    }
38	  }
39	
40	  Future<void> writeAll(List<Entry> entries) {
41	    final encoded = jsonEncode(entries.map(_toJson).toList());
42	    return _storage.write(key: _key, value: encoded);
43	  }
44	
45	  Map<String, dynamic> _toJson(Entry e) => {
46	    'id': e.id,
47	    'content': e.content,
48	    'source': e.source.name,
49	    'chatMessageId': e.chatMessageId,
50	    'occurredAt': e.occurredAt.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
51	    'tags': [
52	      for (final tag in e.tags) {'id': tag.id, 'name': tag.name},
53	    ],
54	    'piiStatus': e.piiStatus.name,
55	    'piiSpans': [
56	      for (final span in e.piiSpans)
57	        {'start': span.start, 'end': span.end, 'type': span.type},
58	    ],
59	    'embeddingStatus': e.embeddingStatus.name,
60	    'mediaDurationSeconds': e.mediaDurationSeconds,
61	    'serverRevision': e.serverRevision,
62	    'createdAt': e.createdAt.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
63	    'updatedAt': e.updatedAt.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
64	    'similarity': e.similarity,
65	  };
66	
67	  Entry _fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> data) => Entry(
68	    id: data['id'] as String,
69	    content: data['content'] as String,
70	    source: EntrySource.values.byName(data['source'] as String),
71	    chatMessageId: data['chatMessageId'] as String?,
72	    occurredAt: DateTime.parse(data['occurredAt'] as String),
73	    tags: (data['tags'] as List<dynamic>)
74	        .map(
75	          (t) => EntryTag(
76	            id: (t as Map<String, dynamic>)['id'] as String,
77	            name: t['name'] as String,
78	          ),
79	        )
80	        .toList(),
81	    piiStatus: PiiStatus.values.byName(data['piiStatus'] as String),
82	    piiSpans: (data['piiSpans'] as List<dynamic>)
83	        .map(
84	          (s) => PiiSpan(
85	            start: (s as Map<String, dynamic>)['start'] as int,
86	            end: s['end'] as int,
87	            type: s['type'] as String,
88	          ),
89	        )
90	        .toList(),
91	    embeddingStatus: EmbeddingStatus.values.byName(
92	      data['embeddingStatus'] as String,
93	    ),
94	    mediaDurationSeconds: data['mediaDurationSeconds'] as int?,
95	    serverRevision: data['serverRevision'] as int,
96	    createdAt: DateTime.parse(data['createdAt'] as String),
97	    updatedAt: DateTime.parse(data['updatedAt'] as String),
98	    similarity: (data['similarity'] as num?)?.toDouble(),
99	  );
100	}

6	/// The shared seam research.md R8 builds because requirements.md §RF10
7	/// already names it (contracts/entries-repository.md). Registered as a
8	/// `get_it` `lazySingleton` so [cachedEntries] survives across modal opens
9	/// (same lifetime pattern as RF03's `VaultRepository`).
10	abstract class EntriesRepository {
11	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({
12	    required String content,
13	    required EntrySource source,
14	    String? chatMessageId,
15	    DateTime? occurredAt,
16	  });
17	
18	  /// FR-011's "local entries store/cache" — every entry this app has ever
19	  /// successfully fetched or created, backed by on-device persistence so it
20	  /// survives a restart. `RecordsBloc` reads this back out as the offline
21	  /// fallback when a fetch fails outright (the PRD's "local read cache",
22	  /// requirements.md line 50/125).
23	  List<Entry> get cachedEntries;
24	
25	  /// `GET /entries` (`entries-list`), paginated newest-occurred-first.
26	  /// Retries exactly once through `SessionRepository.refresh()` on
27	  /// `AuthExpiredFailure` before giving up (research.md R4).
28	  Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({
29	    String? cursor,
30	    EntrySource? source,
31	    DateTime? dateFrom,
32	    DateTime? dateTo,
33	    int? limit,
34	  });
35	
36	  /// `GET /entries/:id` (`entries-get`). Implemented and tested; no call
37	  /// site in this unit's UI flow (research.md R7).
38	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> getById(String id);
39	
40	  /// `GET /entries/search` (`entries-search`) — bounded, no cursor
41	  /// (FR-005b). Retries exactly once through `SessionRepository.refresh()`
42	  /// on `AuthExpiredFailure`, same as `list()`/`getById()`.
43	  Future<Either<Failure, List<Entry>>> search({
44	    String? q,
45	    EntrySource? source,
46	    DateTime? dateFrom,
47	    DateTime? dateTo,
48	    int limit = 50,
49	  });
50	}

1	import 'package:cerne/core/network/failure.dart';
2	import 'package:cerne/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_message.dart';
3	import 'package:cerne/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_session.dart';
4	import 'package:cerne/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_sessions_page.dart';
5	import 'package:cerne/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_stream_event.dart';
6	import 'package:cerne/features/chat/domain/entities/insight_trigger.dart';
7	import 'package:fpdart/fpdart.dart';
8	
9	/// The shared seam `ChatBloc`/`ChatSessionsBloc` depend on (data-model.md,
10	/// contracts/chat-repository.md). Registered as a `get_it` `lazySingleton`
11	/// so [cachedSessions]/[cachedMessages] survive across screen rebuilds.
12	abstract class ChatRepository {
13	  /// `POST /chat/sessions` (`chat-sessions-create`). Retries exactly once
14	  /// through `SessionRepository.refresh()` on `AuthExpiredFailure` (same
15	  /// shape as every other non-streaming call in this codebase).
16	  Future<Either<Failure, ChatSession>> createSession({required String title});
17	
18	  /// `GET /chat/sessions` (`chat-sessions-list`), ordered by
19	  /// `lastUserMessageAt` desc (FR-008).
20	  Future<Either<Failure, ChatSessionsPage>> listSessions({
21	    String? cursor,
22	    int? limit,
23	  });
24	
25	  /// Every session returned by any successful [listSessions] call this
26	  /// process has made, backed by `ChatLocalCache` so it survives a restart
27	  /// (research.md R4) — the offline fallback `ChatSessionsBloc` reads when a
28	  /// fetch fails outright.
29	  List<ChatSession> get cachedSessions;
30	
31	  /// `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` (`chat-messages-list`), ordered by
32	  /// `seq`.
33	  Future<Either<Failure, List<ChatMessage>>> listMessages(String sessionId);
34	
35	  /// The last successfully-fetched message list for [sessionId], or `null`
36	  /// if this session's history has never been fetched while online
37	  /// (research.md R4/Clarification 3) — `null` is the signal `ChatBloc` uses
38	  /// to show the "standard no-connection state" instead of any content when
39	  /// selecting it while offline.
40	  List<ChatMessage>? cachedMessages(String sessionId);
41	
42	  /// Persists which conversation to resume on next app open
43	  /// (spec.md Assumptions).
44	  Future<void> setLastActiveSessionId(String? sessionId);
45	  Future<String?> get lastActiveSessionId;
46	
47	  /// `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages` (`chat-messages-send`), SSE. Retries
48	  /// the whole call exactly once via `SessionRepository.refresh()` only if
49	  /// the very first emitted item is `AuthExpiredFailure` (research.md R3).
50	  Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>> sendMessage({
51	    required String sessionId,
52	    required String content,
53	  });
54	
55	  /// `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry`
56	  /// (`chat-messages-retry`), SSE. Same retry-once-if-first-frame-fails
57	  /// shape as [sendMessage] (research.md R3).
58	  Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>> retryMessage({
59	    required String sessionId,
60	    required String userMessageId,
61	  });
62	
63	  /// FR-008's device-local, best-effort "already saved" record, keyed by
64	  /// `ChatMessage.id`. Not the source of correctness (research.md R1) — the
65	  /// backend's own `entries-create` idempotency is. Safe to read only after
66	  /// this session's local-cache load has resolved, the same guarantee every
67	  /// other `ChatRepositoryImpl` method already awaits internally.
68	  String? savedEntryIdFor(String chatMessageId);
69	
70	  /// Persists [entryId] against [chatMessageId] in the record above — called
71	  /// once per successful chat-sourced entry creation.
72	  Future<void> recordMessageSaved({
73	    required String chatMessageId,
74	    required String entryId,
75	  });
76	
77	  /// `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight` (`chat-insight-create`). `Right(content)`
78	  /// only for `status: 'ready'`; every other outcome — a transport failure,
79	  /// or a 200 response with `status: 'failed'` — is `Left` (research.md R7).
80	  /// Retries once via `SessionRepository.refresh()` on `AuthExpiredFailure`,
81	  /// the same shape as every other non-streaming call (research.md R7).
82	  /// Never reads or writes any local cache — nothing about an insight is
83	  /// ever persisted (FR-009).
84	  Future<Either<Failure, String>> createInsight({
85	    required String sessionId,
86	    required InsightTriggerType triggerType,
87	    required String triggerKey,
88	  });
89	}

## Completion Report

Implemented P-RF09 (Settings Dashboard) end-to-end across all three user stories:

**Foundational (Phase 2):** New `settings/domain/` entities (`DashboardAggregate` + `tenBars()` bucketing, `DashboardNarrative`, `AccountProfile`), 3 repository interfaces, the settings-owned biometric usecase, plus additive `logout()`/`clearLocalData()` methods on `auth`/`entries`/`chat`.

**US1 — Dashboard (P1):** `DashboardRepository`/`DashboardRemoteDataSource`/`DashboardRepositoryImpl`, `SettingsBloc` (covering all three stories' events in one build), and the chart/card/narrative widgets.

**US2 — Account deletion (P1):** `AccountDeletionRepository` stack, the destructive confirmation dialog, double-tap guard, and the full local-data wipe (session, cached profile, entries, chat).

**US3 — Profile/biometric/sign-out (P2):** `AccountProfileRepository` stack with Keychain-backed caching, the profile header with inline name editing, the biometric toggle (await-then-revert), "Sair", and `AppDrawer` now reads the real cached display name instead of its email-derived stand-in.

**Wiring:** `SettingsPage` replaces the placeholder in `app_router.dart`; ~14 new DI registrations in `service_locator.dart`; placeholder page deleted.

- `flutter analyze`: 0 issues
- `flutter test`: 659/659 passing (added ~130 new tests across domain, data, and bloc layers)
